title: Trolling
text: After capturing Itsuki alive and making our escape, we repurposed the hideout of the bandits we’d defeated while traveling as merchants and locked him up there. After all, to take Itsuki away through the portal, we’d have to add him to our party. I couldn’t imagine this Itsuki ever agreeing to join us. So, after making sure he was sound asleep, I had Kou and Yuki-chan keep watch while I summoned my Father.
“Motoyasu-kun…”
Seeing Itsuki lying there in a room at the hideout, my Father put his hand to his forehead in exasperation and groaned.
“Who told you to capture Itsuki alive?”
“Oh? I thought I mentioned it before, but maybe I was just imagining things?”
“I told you it would be problematic given my position! Oh, for heaven’s sake… So? Why did you ask Gaelion-chan to come, too?”
“Gau?”
My Father has brought along my Rival, his Assistant, and Keel. Keel is sneakily peeking into the room and muttering things like, “Whoa!”
“I have some reservations about this, but I’d like my Rival to cast the Dragon’s Sanctuary Magic.”
“What will happen if he does?”
“It’ll allow us to interfere with the teleportation skill. Mind you, even I could do it—but if it’s cast several times, it’ll eventually break through.”

It’s Magic that affects the surrounding Magical Power field, after all. Since it’s just a matter of boosting the power—or making a minor Magic more potent—it doesn’t have that much of an impact on the Magical Power field. So even if we can temporarily block its use, it’ll become usable again right away.
“I see. Well then, Gaelion, could you do that for us?”
“Leave it to me!”
That’s what my rival said. The Assistant was holding up a finger to signal “shh.”
“…Did she talk?”
I thought my rival could already speak? Oh, you mean the physical version of my rival?
“Yeah! I was talking with Wyndia-nee about keeping it a secret so we could surprise you.”
She’s wagging her tail and flaunting her cuteness right in my face. It makes me want to puke.
“H-huh…”
“Naofumi, are you surprised?”
“I’m surprised, I’m surprised.”
“I am, I am! We did it! Now, Father’s—No? Oh well… that’s too bad.”
Father nodded as if he’d guessed what the Rival was about to say. The Assistant is tilting her head in confusion.
“W-well then, Gaelion-chan, please.”
“Got it!”

The rival began casting Magic to create a sanctuary. Normally, the Filolial-samas would be able to cast it as well, but starting with Yuki-chan, none of them can use it yet. So, out of necessity, they created the sanctuary to prevent Itsuki from escaping.
“Dragon Sanctuary!”
However, the downside is that this Magic asserts that this is a dragon’s territory, which causes stress for the Filolial-samas.
“With this, Itsuki can no longer escape through the portal.”
“That’s fine, but what do we do now? We can’t exactly move our hideout to Melromarc…”
“We just need to keep Itsuki confined and protect him. That way, the chances of Itsuki dying will be virtually zero.”
Even if Takt and his crew attack, we can fight them off.
“Why not throw Ren in there with Itsuuki, too?”
“If you throw Ren in there too, things will just get even more complicated!”
My Father scolded me. I thought it was a brilliant idea, though.
“For now… let’s try talking to Itsuki.”
“That’s right.”
We went to see Itsuki, who was lying in a room at our hideout. Perhaps the effects of the sleep skill were still wearing off—Itsuki was fast asleep. He looked rather pathetic.
“I guess I’ll just give Itsuuki a little shake to wake him up.”
Father sat Itsuki—whom I’d tied up and muzzled so he couldn’t speak—in a chair and made sure he could talk. Then he gave him a gentle shake to wake him up.
“W-where… am I…?”
Itsuki, who had been dazed, glared at Father as his consciousness cleared.
“Naofumi! Where is this?! What are you planning to do to me?!”
“I don’t plan on doing anything, really. I mean… that’s the first thing you say as soon as you wake up…”
My Father replied with a sigh. He has no intention of making you do anything. The most he’d ask of you is to just sit still and do nothing.
“These ropes!”
Realizing he was tied up, Itsuki tried to cast a spell. But I immediately interrupted him.
“Whoa, you’d better not think you can cut these ropes with magic.”
It’s easy enough to block magic at Itsuki’s level. Even an Assistant could block a spell like this. After all, Itsuki’s magic is low-performance magic he learned from the crystal.
“Guh… Teleportation Bow! Wait a minute!? I can’t teleport!”
“That’s useless, too. It’s easy to block.”
“Guh…”

Itsuki glares at us with all his might. Hahaha, that look doesn’t scare me one bit. Did you really think we hadn’t prepared countermeasures? Just as Jyu was preparing for those pointless status effects, we’ve been taking our own precautions. It’s a foolish notion to assume an enemy will remain at the same strength forever.
“Just because you’ve captured me doesn’t mean the country or my comrades will stay silent!”
“Oh? How exactly is a country in shambles from the revolution supposed to save Itsuki? And his comrades, too? Haha, this is a joke.”
Does Itsuki really trust the very people who actively tried to kill him in the last loop? This is ridiculous. It’s pitiful that Itsuki considers such people his comrades.
“What’s so funny?!”
“I bet they’re badmouthing Itsuki right about now. ‘The Bow Hero is weak,’ ‘Isn’t he a fake?’ ‘Gyahaha!’—they’re definitely saying things like that.”
“That’s not true! We’re bound by unbreakable bonds of justice!”
“Ha ha ha! A strong bond of justice! That’s quite something, isn’t it~?”

I laughed as I clapped my hands. So it’s a “strong bond of justice,” is it? It’s truly a bond of justice, isn’t it? Since losing means you’re evil, Itsuki must have been killed. Just as I was grinning to myself, my Father spoke up.
“Why are you provoking Itsuki!”
My Father got angry at me. Now that he mentioned it, why was I provoking Itsuki, anyway? …Maybe it’s because he’s done so many annoying things to me—including during all the loops so far.
“Anyway, won’t you at least listen to what we have to say?”
“I don’t have a mouth for talking to evil! Come on! Release me quickly. Then I’ll spare your lives!”
“Whoa… he’s completely written us off as evil.”
He doesn’t understand his own situation at all. If we weren’t in a loop, I’d be killing you right now.
“It’s obvious! You brainwashed the people and kidnapped Princess Melty! And to top it all off, you’re plotting to overthrow the government! Princess Malty and the King begged me in tears!”
“…Do you seriously think you’re in the right? Itsuki, weren’t you just focused on satisfying your sense of justice without thinking about the consequences?”

“What are you talking about!　Everything I’ve done since coming to this world has been for the greater good! Naofumi! Motoyasu! I’m not doing anything like what you two are doing—inciting a coup d’état!”
“…Sigh.”
My father lets out a deep sigh. I feel the same way, actually.

“Itsuki, you just can’t seem to grasp that these events are the result of actions you believed were for the greater good. Anything that goes against you is ‘brainwashing’? That’s such a cliché and convenient excuse.”
“Of course it is! Come on! Hurry up and break the brainwashing! You Demon King!”

“We don’t have that kind of power. This revolution… is happening because we’re cleaning up the mess you and Ren made, and because of our own actions. Besides, with the world already in such turmoil because of the waves, there’s no way we’d go out of our way to start a revolution.”

“Let’s think this through.” That’s how Father wrapped things up, but Itsuki seemed completely unfazed, as if the words had gone in one ear and out the other. It seems he still hasn’t woken up from his dream yet. Maybe I should give him a good beating—just enough to knock some sense into him without killing him? Nah, a kid like this will snap out of it after a few punches.
“No, that’s a lie. Otherwise, there’s no way the people would be throwing stones at us—the ones who solved the case!”
Even my father looked genuinely annoyed.

“Were you even listening to what people were saying? Because you failed to address the root cause, the number of people suffering from famine and heavy taxes hasn’t gone down, has it? Sure, it feels good to take down the villains you can see, but you didn’t consider that even if you cut off one head, another will grow in its place—this is the result of your short-sighted actions.”
“As expected of the Pillar of Evil—you really do speak differently! But I won’t be fooled!”

My father and Itsuki started glaring at each other fiercely. What a hassle. Maybe I should confine Itsuki—just enough so he doesn’t die… perhaps turn him into a daruma doll or something? If I keep him alive, he won’t cause too much trouble, which might actually make things easier.
“Itsuki, I’ll have you talk to Melty-chan—the Second Princess—later, so I think you should at least start noticing how strange things are in this country.”
“No matter what you say, I won’t believe a word of it.”
“Well then, time for another nap!”
I was annoyed too, so I struck Itsuki with a Sleep Lance.
“Ugh…!”
Even my Father is just standing there silently, watching Itsuki collapse.
